'''Francesco Pocchiari''' (25 June 1924, [[Melfi]] - 2 January 1989, Rome) was an Italian chemist and pharmacologist, researcher in microbiology and biological chemistry. He was the director of the [[Istituto Superiore di Sanità]] between 1972 and 1989. In honor of his memory, the [[Francesco Pocchiari Fellowship]] was established in 1991 with funds provided by the Italian Government.

== Biography ==
Pocchiari was born on 25 June 1924 in [[Melfi]], in the province of [[Potenza]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Alberani |first1=V. |last2=D'Agnolo |first2=G. |last3=Donelli |first3=G. |last4=Silano |first4=V. |date=1990 |title=Francesco Pocchiari: l'uomo, i progetti e le realizzazioni. |url=https://www.iss.it/documents/20126/955767/Art.+06.1129723030.pdf/bc13bbea-e1ea-714e-789d-47c4a3b65065?t=1575580534999 |journal=Annali dell'Istituto Superiore di Sanità |language=Italian |volume=26 Suppl 1 |pages=21–67 |issn=0021-2571 |pmid=2095681}}</ref> He graduated chemistry in 1948 from the [[Sapienza University of Rome]]. He started as a researcher in 1949 at the Laboratory of Chemical Microbiology of the [[Istituto Superiore di Sanità]] together with [[Ernst Chain|Ernst Boris Chain]]. In 1969, he was appointed director of the biological chemistry laboratory of the Istituto Superiore di Sanità and, in 1971, he became a director of the institute, a position he would hold until his death.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=E' SCOMPARSO IERI A ROMA FRANCESCO POCCHIARI - la Repubblica.it |url=https://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1989/01/03/scomparso-ieri-roma-francesco-pocchiari.html |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=Archivio - la Repubblica.it |date=3 January 1989 |language=it}}</ref> During his more than sixteen tenure, Pocchiari faced delicate and serious issues including the [[1973 cholera epidemic in Naples]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=1973-09-05 |title=CHOLERA IN ITALY KILLS 18TH VICTIM |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1973/09/05/archives/cholera-in-italy-kills-18th-victim-the-disease-strikes-for-the.html |access-date=2023-04-19 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> There also he collaborated with [[Rita Levi-Montalcini|Rita Levi Montalcini]] who, together with Pocchiari, carried out fundamental research to guarantee her the [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]] in 1986.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rita Levi-Montalcini - Biography, Facts and Pictures |url=https://www.famousscientists.org/rita-levi-montalcini/ |access-date=2023-04-13 |language=en-US}}</ref> 

In 1954, he also graduated in pharmacy; two years later, he became a professor of applied biochemistry at the Sapienza University of Rome and also taught at the universities of [[University of Bologna|Bologna]] and [[University of Bari|Bari]].<ref name=":02" /> He also writes articles for medical journals such as [[Brain Research]], [[Biochemical Journal]], [[Lancet (journal)|Lancet]], [[Nature (journal)|Nature]] and is a member of Italian and international scientific committees such as the [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) Executive Committee in Geneva, and the European Council for Medical Research in Strasbourg.<ref>{{Cite web |title=History |url=https://www.iss.it/la-nostra-storia |access-date=2023-04-13 |website=ISS |language=en-US}}</ref> Pocchiari's achievements in the field of public health research are documented in the book "Accidental exposure to [[Dioxins and dioxin-like compounds|dioxins]]: human health aspects," which he co-edited with [[Fred Coulston|Frederick Coulston]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Accidental exposure to dioxins : human health aspects / edited by Frederick Coulston, Francesco Pocchiari. |url=https://wellcomecollection.org/works/gtruzb2d |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=Wellcome Collection |language=en}}</ref>

After his death, the Aula Magna of the Istituto Superiore di Sanità was dedicated to him. In honor of his memory, the [[Francesco Pocchiari Fellowship]] was established in 1991 with funds provided by the Italian Government.<ref>{{Cite web |title=WHO {{!}} Public health prizes and awards |url=https://apps.who.int/gb/awards/e/Pocchiari.html |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=apps.who.int}}</ref> This fellowship is administered by the WHO and is awarded to individuals who have made significant contributions to public health research. The fellowship was initially endowed with US$104,960 from the Italian Government.<ref name=":1" />

Pocchiari was married with three children.<ref name=":02" /> He died on 2 January 1989 in Rome.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=E' SCOMPARSO IERI A ROMA FRANCESCO POCCHIARI - la Repubblica.it |url=https://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1989/01/03/scomparso-ieri-roma-francesco-pocchiari.html |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=Archivio - la Repubblica.it |date=3 January 1989 |language=it}}</ref>
